references.text: The prophet Isaiah uses the image of a vineyard to describe the house of Israel and how God looks for justice but finds bloodshed, which mirrors the action against the owner of the vineyard in Mark.
Hosea speaks about how Israel, like a vineyard, will be destroyed because of their wickedness, parallel to the owners of the vineyard in Mark who kill the son.
Jesus tells a similar parable about the owners of the vineyard in Matthew, who kill the son, which directly corresponds with the event in Mark.
Luke gives a parallel account to Mark about the owners of the vineyard who kill the son, emphasizing universal condemnation of this act.
